If a judge decides that possession is not reasonable at this time, they may instead decide to order a demotion of tenancy (demotion order) or a suspension of the defendants’ right to buy (suspension order), if they’re not already in place.

Suspension of right to buy

A suspension order means that the defendants will not have a right to buy the premises during the suspension.

Demotion of tenancy

A demotion order means that the defendants’ current tenancy will be replaced with a demoted tenancy. During this period (usually 12 months) they will lose some rights they currently have. The claimant is able to propose a new set of terms that will be put in place by the demotion order.

Atal yr hawl i brynu

Mae gorchymyn atal yn golygu na fydd gan y diffynnydd hawl i brynu'r eiddo yn ystod cyfnod y gorchymyn atal.

Tenantiaeth isradd

column1:

You may have already given the defendants notice of your intention to begin possession proceedings and written which grounds you’re making the possession claim under. You should select these grounds here.

Serious rent arrears (ground 8)

Mandatory ground. Can be used if the defendants owe at least:

  • eight weeks’ rent if they pay weekly or fortnightly
  • two months’ rent if they pay monthly
  • three months’ rent if they pay quarterly or yearly

The defendants must owe the rent when the notice is served and at the time of the hearing.

Rent arrears (ground 10)

Discretionary ground. The defendants are in any amount of arrears.

Persistent delay in paying rent (ground 11)

Discretionary ground. The defendants have persistently delayed paying their rent.
column2:
---

Efallai eich bod eisoes wedi rhoi hysbysiad i'r diffynnydd o'ch bwriad i ddechrau achos meddiannu ac wedi ysgrifennu ar ba sail rydych yn gwneud yr hawliad. Dylech ddewis y seiliau hyn yma.

Ôl-ddyledion rhent difrifol (sail 8)

Sail gorfodol. Gellir ei ddefnyddio os oes gan y diffynnydd o leiaf ddyled o:

  • wyth wythnos o rent os ydynt yn talu'n wythnosol neu bob pythefnos
  • dau fis o rent os ydynt yn talu'n fisol
  • tri mis o rent os ydynt yn talu'n chwarterol neu'n flynyddol

Rhaid i'r rhent fod yn ddyledus gan y diffynnydd pan gyflwynir yr hysbysiad ac ar adeg y gwrandawiad.

Ôl-ddyledion rhent (sail 10)

Sail dewisol. Mae gan y diffynnydd unrhyw faint o ôl-ddyledion.

Oedi cyson wrth dalu rhent (sail 11)

Sail yn ôl disgresiwn. Mae'r diffynnydd wedi oedi cyn talu rhent yn gyson.

column1:

The rent statement must show:

  • every date when a payment was supposed to be made
  • the amount that was due on each of those dates
  • the actual payments that were made, and when they were made
  • the total rent arrears

It must cover the time period of either:

  • from the first date the defendants missed a payment, or
  • the last two years of payments, if the first date of their missed payment was more than two years ago

column1:
Your claim will be saved as you answer the questions, so you’ll be able to close and return to your draft. Before you submit, you must complete a statement of truth. This certifies that you believe the information you’ve provided is true.

What you’ll need

Before you start, make sure you have the following information:

  • details of the tenancy, contract, licence or mortgage agreement
  • the defendants’ details (the people you’re making the claim against)
  • your reasons for making a possession claim
  • copies of any relevant documents. You can either upload documents now or closer to the hearing date. Any documents you upload now will be included in the pack of documents that a judge will receive before the hearing (the bundle)

Completing your claim

Once you’ve finished answering the questions, you can either:

  • sign, submit and pay for your claim now, or
  • save it as a draft. You or someone else can then return to sign, submit and pay at a later date
column2:
Bydd eich hawliad yn cael ei gadw wrth i chi ateb y cwestiynau, felly gallwch ei gau a dychwelyd at eich drafft. Cyn ei gyflwyno, mae'n rhaid ichi gwblhau datganiad gwirionedd. Mae hyn yn tystio eich bod yn credu bod yr wybodaeth a ddarperir gennych yn wir.

Yr hyn fyddwch ei angen

Cyn dechrau, gwnewch yn siŵr fod gennych yr wybodaeth ganlynol:

  • manylion y denantiaeth, contract, trwydded neu gytundeb morgais
  • manylion y diffynyddion (y bobl rydych yn gwneud yr hawliad yn eu herbyn)
  • eich rhesymau dros wneud hawliad meddiannu
  • copïau o unrhyw ddogfennau perthnasol. Gallwch naill ai uwchlwytho dogfennau nawr neu'n agosach at ddyddiad y gwrandawiad. Caiff unrhyw ddogfennau y byddwch yn eu huwchlwytho nawr eu cynnwys yn y pecyn o ddogfennau y bydd barnwr yn ei gael cyn y gwrandawiad (y bwndel)

Cwblhau eich hawliad

Unwaith y byddwch wedi gorffen ateb y cwestiynau, gallwch naill ai:

  • llofnodi, cyflwyno a thalu am eich hawliad nawr, neu
  • ei gadw fel drafft. Yna, gallwch chi neu rywun arall ddychwelyd i lofnodi, cyflwyno a thalu yn nes ymlaen

column1:

You can use this online service if you’re a registered provider of social housing or a community landlord and the property you want to claim possession of is in England or Wales.

Solicitors or legal representatives must continue to submit claims using Possession Claim Online (PCOL) or by using a claim form with the relevant particulars of claim form.

This service is also available in Welsh (Cymraeg).

You cannot continue with your application until you have asked the judge for permission to make this change.

column1:
The bailiff has arranged a date for the eviction and they need you to confirm if you are available.

They will also ask you to confirm if the person being evicted poses any risk.

The bailiff needs this information to carry out the eviction safely. If you do not provide it, they may not be able to complete the eviction.

What you’ll need

You’ll need to know:

  • who will attend the eviction (you, or someone else)
  • if you (or they) can attend the eviction on the date suggested by the bailiff

We will also ask you to:

  • describe the person who will be evicted
  • tell us how to access the property
  • book a locksmith (this is to make sure that the person being evicted cannot return to the property)

Once you have confirmed the eviction date, we’ll send you an email reminding you to book a locksmith.

column1:
I do not know if I need to hire a High Court enforcement officer

A High Court enforcement officer (HCEO) is a type of bailiff. If your application for a writ is successful, a High Court enforcement officer will carry out the eviction.

You can either choose your own HCEO, or we will choose one for you. The cost is the same, but if you have not chosen one then you will need to send a copy of your writ to the National Enforcement Office (we’ll send you an email explaining where to send it to).

If you want to choose your own High Court enforcement officer

It usually costs around £1000.00 to hire a High Court enforcement officer to do an eviction.

You may need to pay additional fees for things like:

  • hiring a dog handler (if you are trying to evict someone who owns an aggressive dog)
  • hiring a locksmith to secure the property

You can either:

  • search for a High Court enforcement officer using your postcode
  • check the full list of High Court enforcement officers and choose one in your area
  • search for an HCEO using a search engine

We’ll ask you to provide the name of your High Court enforcement officer on the next page.

column1:
I do not know if I need a writ or a warrant

You can use either a warrant or a writ to evict someone.

If you choose a warrant of possession

If you apply for a warrant:

  • it costs ${warrantFeeAmount} to apply
  • it’s free to hire a County Court bailiff
  • you may have to wait longer for the eviction (this depends on the court you apply to)

If you ask the judge for a writ of possession

It’s usually faster to evict someone using a writ, but:

  • it’s more difficult to prove that you need a writ
  • it’s an extra step in the legal process

You’ll need to:

  • ask the judge for a writ (you’ll need additional evidence for this and the judge could still refuse your request)
  • hire a private High Court Enforcement Officer (bailiff) to carry out the eviction

If you apply for a writ:

  • it costs ${writFeeAmount} to apply
  • you can get a quote from a bailiff to find out how much it will cost (they usually charge by the hour)
  • it’s usually faster (6 to 12 weeks, depending on the court you apply to)

The additional evidence you’ll need to apply for a writ

You’ll need to show that either:

  • there is a backlog in the County Court bailiff service
  • the defendant (the person or people living at the property) has damaged your property
  • you are suffering financially due to lost income

If you do not have this evidence the judge could deny your request. If they deny it, you’ll need to start again (re-apply for the writ or the warrant with new evidence).

Contact a lawyer or a High Court Enforcement Officer (bailiff) before you apply for a writ. They can help you to check if you have the evidence to apply successfully.

column1: You can upload a document to support an application, a counterclaim, or to show proof that you have done something. We usually share anything you upload with the other parties, for example other defendants, the defendant’s landlord, housing association or mortgage provider. If your application is ‘without notice’ (where you have asked us to consider your application without telling the other party) we will not share anything with them. What you can upload. You can upload any documents that you think are rel evant.For example, you can share:evidence that a judge has asked for, like bank statements showing your rent payments, photographs of the property in a state of disrepair, like damp in the bathroom, a report from an electrician or a plumber, showing evidence of a repair that needs to be done emails or letters from the claimant (the defendant’s landlord, housing association, or mortgage lender)You can upload the following file types:DOC/DOCX(Word), XLS/XLSM(Excel),PPT/PPTX(PowerPoint),PDF,RTF,TXT,CSV,JPG/JPEG,PNG,BMP,TIF/TIFF. You cannot upload video or audio files.

Trespass claim

A trespass claim can be made against someone who:

  • entered or remained in the property without your consent
  • is not a tenant, sub-tenant or licensee (even if a tenancy or licence has ended)

This includes someone who:

  • had the licence terminated
  • who has no right to occupy because they did not succeed to the tenancy after a death

---

Community landlords should follow the pre-action protocol before making a housing possession claim. You should have:

  • contacted, or attempted to contact, the defendants

If your claim is on the grounds of rent arrears, you should have:

  • tried to agree a repayment plan
  • applied for arrears to be paid by the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) by deductions from the defendants’ benefits
  • offered to assist the defendants in a claim for housing benefit or Universal Credit
! Warning Your case could be delayed or rejected if you have not followed the pre-action protocol and completed all the steps.
column2:

Os yw eich hawliad ar sail ôl-ddyledion rhent, dylech fod wedi:

  • ceisio cytuno ar gynllun ad-dalu

column1:
---

If you need to ask the court for something before your case can be given a hearing date or sent to the defendants, you’ll need to make an application.

Applications could include:

  • permission to make your claim
  • permission to send papers to a defendant outside England or Wales
  • a request for a hearing without notifying the defendants

After you submit and pay for your claim, you’ll have 24 hours to make your application. If you do it any later, a hearing date might be scheduled automatically and your application will be considered by the court separately. It might not be considered or listed before the scheduled first hearing date.

If you’re not sure whether you need to make an application as part of your claim, you should get legal advice.

column1:
The ‘other parties’ are the other people or organisations named on the claim form. For example a tenant, landlord, housing association, or mortgage lender.

Every other party will need to agree to let you make this application, if they don’t agree, you may need to pay a higher fee.

If the other parties do not agree

The application fee will increase to ${xui_genapp_MaxFee} if:

  • you have already told the other party that they are making this application, and
  • the other party did not agree to it (this means that they objected to it)

You’ll see the final application fee before you pay.

What you need to do

You will need to upload evidence for the court, to show that:

  • you have told the other parties, and
  • they agreed to it

For example a copy of a letter, email or a signed consent order. We will ask you to upload this evidence later in this application.

If you were not able to contact the other parties, or you attempted to contact them but the other party did not respond, select ‘No’.
column2:
Y 'partïon eraill' yw'r bobl neu'r sefydliadau eraill a enwir ar y ffurflen hawlio. Er enghraifft, tenant, landlord, cymdeithas dai neu fenthyciwr morgeisi.

Bydd angen i bob parti arall gytuno i adael i chi wneud y cais hwn. Os na fyddant, mae'n bosib y bydd angen i chi dalu ffi uwch.

Os na fydd y partïon eraill yn cytuno

Bydd ffi'r cais yn cynyddu i ${xui_genapp_MaxFee} os:

  • ydych eisoes wedi dweud wrth y parti arall eu bod yn gwneud y cais hwn, ac
  • ni wnaeth y parti arall gytuno iddo (mae hyn yn golygu eu bod wedi ei wrthwynebu)

Byddwch yn gweld y ffi gwneud cais terfynol cyn i chi dalu.

Beth sydd angen i chi ei wneud

Bydd angen i chi uwchlwytho tystiolaeth i'r llys i ddangos:

  • eich bod wedi dweud wrth y partïon eraill, a'u bod
  • wedi cytuno iddo

Er enghraifft copi o lythyr, e-bost neu orchymyn cydsynio wedi'i lofnodi. Byddwn yn gofyn i chi uwchlwytho'r dystiolaeth hon yn hwyrach ymlaen yn y cais hwn.

Os nad oeddech chi'n gallu cysylltu â'r partïon eraill, neu os gwnaethoch geisio cysylltu â nhw ond na wnaeth y parti arall ymateb, dewiswch 'Na'.

column1:
If the other parties do not agree

We usually send a copy of the application to the other parties (the tenant, landlord, housing association or mortgage lender). This gives the other party the opportunity to respond to it.

In some exceptional circumstances, the judge will consider the application without telling the other party first.

For example, if:

  • it is so urgent that there is not enough time to give notice
  • giving someone notice could undermine the order that you want the court to grant
  • you believe that you or your client are at risk from the other party
! Warning We will ask you to provide the reason. The court will consider the reason, and you may not be successful.
column2:

Mewn rhai amgylchiadau eithriadol, bydd y barnwr yn ystyried y cais heb hysbysu'r parti arall yn gyntaf.

Er enghraifft:

  • os yw mor frys fel nad oes digon o amser i roi gwybod am y cais
  • gallai hysbysu rhywun danseilio'r gorchymyn rydych eisiau i'r llys ei ganiatáu
  • rydych yn credu eich bod chi neu eich cleient mewn perygl gan y parti arall
! Rhybudd Byddwn yn gofyn i chi roi'r rheswm. Bydd y llys yn ystyried y rheswm, ac efallai na fyddwch yn llwyddiannus.

column1:
You can ask the court to adjourn (delay) the court hearing (move it to a later date or time). This means that you can ask to change the date and time when the hearing is due to take place.

You will need to provide a good reason to delay the hearing, and you may not be successful.

What you’ll need to apply

You’ll need to know:

  • why you are asking the court to delay the hearing
  • when you are proposing the hearing be moved to (if applicable)

You may need to provide some evidence for the court.

Before you start

Make sure that you have all of the evidence you need to apply.

Once you start the application, you cannot save your progress as a draft.

This means that if you leave the application before submitting, we will not save your answers so that you can return to them later.

How long it takes

Your application will be assessed on an urgency basis and will be considered by a judge before the hearing date.

How much it will cost

It’s free to apply if the court hearing is at least 14 days away.

If your court hearing is sooner, you will need to pay ${xui_genapp_StandardFee}.

The fee will increase to ${xui_genapp_MaxFee} if:

  • you have already told the other party that you are making this application, and
  • the other party did not agree to it (this means that they objected to it)

You’ll see the final application fee before you pay.

  • send the completed form to the court

column1:
The ‘other party’ is the other side involved in the defendant’s case. For example their landlord, housing association, or mortgage lender.

Every other party will need to agree to let them make this application, if they don’t agree, the defendant may need to pay a higher fee.

If the other parties do not agree

The application fee will increase to ${xui_genapp_MaxFee} if:

  • the defendant has already told the other party that they are making this application, and
  • the other party did not agree to it (this means that they objected to it)

You’ll see the final application fee before you pay.

What you need to do

You will need to upload evidence for the court, to show that:

  • the defendant has told the other parties, and
  • they agreed to it

For example a copy of a letter, email or a signed consent order. We will ask you to upload this evidence later in this application.

If the defendant was not able to contact the other parties, or they attempted to contact them but the other party did not respond, select ‘No’.
column2:

Bydd angen i bob parti arall gytuno i adael iddynt wneud y cais hwn. Os na fyddant yn cytuno, mae'n bosib y bydd rhaid i'r diffynnydd dalu ffi uwch.

Os na fydd y partïon eraill yn cytuno

Bydd ffi'r cais yn cynyddu i ${xui_genapp_MaxFee} os:

  • bydd y diffynnydd eisoes wedi dweud wrth y parti arall eu bod yn gwneud y cais hwn, ac
  • ni wnaeth y parti arall gytuno iddo (mae hyn yn golygu eu bod wedi ei wrthwynebu)

Byddwch yn gweld y ffi gwneud cais terfynol cyn i chi dalu.

Bydd angen i chi uwchlwytho tystiolaeth i'r llys i ddangos:

  • bod y diffynnydd wedi dweud wrth y partïon eraill, a'u bod
  • wedi cytuno iddo

Os nad oedd y diffynnydd yn gallu cysylltu â'r partïon eraill, neu os gwnaethant geisio cysylltu â nhw ond na wnaeth y parti arall ymateb, dewiswch 'Na'.

column1:
If the other parties do not agree

We usually send a copy of the application to the other parties (the defendant’s landlord, housing association or mortgage lender). This gives the other party the opportunity to respond to it.

In some exceptional circumstances, the judge will consider the application without telling the other party first.

For example, if:

  • it is so urgent that there is not enough time for the defendant to give notice
  • giving someone notice could undermine the order that the defendant wants the court to grant
  • the defendant believes that they are at risk from the other party
! Warning We will ask you to provide the reason. The court will consider the reason, and the defendant may not be successful.
column2:
Os na fydd y partïon eraill yn cytuno

Fel arfer rydym yn anfon copi o'r cais at y partïon eraill (landlord, cymdeithas dai neu fenthyciwr morgeisi y diffynnydd). Mae hyn yn rhoi cyfle i'r parti arall ymateb iddo.

Mewn rhai amgylchiadau eithriadol, bydd y barnwr yn ystyried y cais heb hysbysu'r parti arall yn gyntaf.

Er enghraifft, os:

  • yw mor frys fel nad oes digon o amser i'r diffynnydd roi gwybod am y cais
  • gallai hysbysu rhywun danseilio'r gorchymyn y mae'r diffynnydd eisiau i'r llys ei ganiatáu
  • mae'r diffynnydd yn credu eu bod mewn perygl gan y parti arall
! Rhybudd Byddwn yn gofyn i chi roi'r rheswm. Bydd y llys yn ystyried y rheswm, ac efallai na fydd y diffynnydd yn llwyddiannus.

column1:
You can ask the court to adjourn (delay) the defendant’s court hearing (move it to a later date or time). This means that you can ask to change the date and time when the hearing is due to take place.

You will need to show that the defendant has a good reason to delay the hearing, and they may not be successful.

What you’ll need to apply

You’ll need to know:

  • if the defendant can pay the court fee, or if they need Help with Fees (help to pay court fees)
  • why the defendant is asking the court to delay the hearing
  • when they are proposing the hearing be moved to (if applicable)

They may need to provide some evidence for the court.

Before you start

Make sure that you have all of the evidence you need to apply.

Once you start the application, you cannot save your progress as a draft.

This means that if you leave the application before submitting, we will not save your answers so that you can return to them later.

How long it takes

Your application will be assessed on an urgency basis and will be considered by a judge before the hearing date.

How much it will cost

It’s free to apply if the defendant’s court hearing is at least 14 days away.

If your court hearing is sooner, they will need to pay ${xui_genapp_StandardFee}.

The fee will increase to ${xui_genapp_MaxFee} if:

  • the defendant has already told the other party that they are making this application, and
  • the other party did not agree to it (this means that they objected to it)

You’ll see the final application fee before you pay.

If you are worried about the defendant paying fees

They may be eligible to apply for help with fees (GOV.UK, opens in a new tab). We will ask you if they want to do this when you apply.

Apply by post

You cannot apply to suspend (stop or delay) the eviction online.

You must apply by post:

  • fill in the N244 form
  • find the defendant’s local court
  • send the completed form to the court

You can upload a document to support an application, or to show proof that you have done something.

We usually share anything you upload with the other party, for example your tenant or the mortgage payer.

If your application is ‘without notice’ (where you have asked us to consider your application without telling the other party) we will not share anything with them.

What you can upload

You can upload any documents that you think are relevant.

For example, you can share:

  • proof that you have cancelled an eviction
  • evidence that a judge has asked for, like a witness statement, or a tenancy agreement
  • an inspection of the property, or a report done by a surveyor
  • photographs of damage to the property
  • letters, emails and text messages from the defendant

You can ask the court to adjourn (delay) the court hearing (move it to a later date or time). This means that you can ask to change the date and time when the hearing is due to take place.

You will need to provide a good reason to delay the hearing, and you may not be successful.

What you’ll need to apply

You’ll need to know:

  • why you are asking the court to delay the hearing
  • when you are proposing the hearing be moved to (if applicable)

You may need to provide some evidence for the court.

Before you start

Make sure that you have all of the evidence you need to apply.

Once you start the application, you cannot save your progress as a draft.

This means that if you leave the application before submitting, we will not save your answers so that you can return to them later.

How long it takes

Your application will be assessed on an urgency basis and will be considered by a judge before the hearing date.

How much it will cost

It’s free to apply if the court hearing is at least 14 days away.

column1:
You can ask the court to adjourn (delay) the defendant’s court hearing (move it to a later date or time). This means that you can ask to change the date and time when the hearing is due to take place.

You will need to show that the defendant has a good reason to delay the hearing, and they may not be successful.

What you’ll need to apply

You’ll need to know:

  • if the defendant can pay the court fee, or if they need Help with Fees (help to pay court fees)
  • why the defendant is asking the court to delay the hearing
  • when they are proposing the hearing be moved to (if applicable)

They may need to provide some evidence for the court.

Before you start

Make sure that you have all of the evidence you need to apply.

Once you start the application, you cannot save your progress as a draft.

This means that if you leave the application before submitting, we will not save your answers so that you can return to them later.

How long it takes

Your application will be assessed on an urgency basis and will be considered by a judge before the hearing date.

How much it will cost

It’s free to apply if the defendant’s court hearing is at least 14 days away.
